app_purpose: Python WSGI request/response library. When application code sets Response.location to a user-controlled value for an HTTP redirect (302), WebOb normalizes the Location header to an absolute URL at WSGI __call__ time (Response._abs_headerlist -> _make_location_absolute). That normalization is where WebOb must neutralize protocol-relative / off-origin targets to prevent an open redirect.
sink: src/webob/response.py :: Response._make_location_absolute (invoked via _abs_headerlist on __call__). The prior fix rewrites values that literally startswith('//') to '/%2f...'; the residual bypasses it because urllib.parse.urlsplit (called by urljoin) strips ASCII tab/CR/LF on Python 3.10+, re-forming '//attacker' after the check.
run_mode_note: Real-library-wrap. Each version profile boots the SAME tiny real WSGI app (wsgi_app.py) on python:3.11-slim with the REAL pip-installed WebOb bytes (WebOb==1.8.7 / 1.8.8 / 1.8.10). No WebOb code is copied or reimplemented; the redirect-target normalization is executed entirely by the installed webob package. The open redirect is triggered EXTERNALLY over HTTP (GET /redirect?to=<payload>) and the observable is the REAL Location response header WebOb emits. python:3.11 is required because the CVE-2026-44889 residual depends on the Python 3.10+ urlsplit() tab/CR/LF stripping behavior.

v0.ref: real pip WebOb 1.8.7; _make_location_absolute has NO anti-open-redirect normalization

v1.ref: real pip WebOb 1.8.8; CVE-2024-42353 fix present (startswith('//') -> '/%2f...'); CVE-2026-44889 tab-strip residual still open

v2.ref: real pip WebOb 1.8.10; CVE-2026-44889 fix (strips \t\r\n before the SCHEME_RE / '//' checks)

real_flow.app: wsgi_app.py: GET /redirect?to=<input> -> Response(status=302, location=<input>); WebOb makes the Location absolute on __call__.
real_flow.observable: the Location header of the 302 response emitted by the REAL WebOb Response.
real_flow.control: a benign relative redirect_to=/explore yields Location: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/explore on all three versions, proving the redirect is genuinely honored (so a same-origin Location is a real normalization block, not a failed request).

flag.resource: the redirect target (Location header) emitted by the REAL WebOb Response after normalization
flag.placement: redirect-canary: per-run ${PCB_FLAG} is used as the path label inside the attacker redirect host (to=//attacker.pcb/${PCB_FLAG} or to=/\t/attacker.pcb/${PCB_FLAG}); the FLAG reaches the emitted Location on an attacker HOST iff WebOb's normalization is bypassed. Blocked -> Location stays same-origin (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/%2fattacker.pcb/...), attacker host absent. Nothing planted in app code or data.
flag.detect: parse the Location header; OPEN redirect iff resolved host == 'attacker.pcb' (off the server origin) AND ${PCB_FLAG} present in Location.

given_to_method: docker-compose.yml (boots REAL WebOb 1.8.8 as the v1 target)

evidence.fix_reference: real pip WebOb 1.8.8; CVE-2024-42353 fix present (startswith('//') -> '/%2f...'); CVE-2026-44889 tab-strip residual still open; real pip WebOb 1.8.10; CVE-2026-44889 fix (strips \t\r\n before the SCHEME_RE / '//' checks)
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: urlsplit() (called internally by urljoin) treats a '//' at the start of a string as a URI without a scheme. The CVE-2024-42353 fix replaced a literal leading '//', but failed to account for Python 3.10+ urlsplit() stripping ASCII tab, carriage return, and newline: a '/\t/attacker.com' target passes the '//' check unchanged, then urlsplit strips the tab -> '//attacker.com', bringing back the problem that was attempted to be fixed.
